review.algorithm_assessment: The completed graph is one spanning ring, with degree exactly two at every vertex (a loop contributes two and n=2 may use parallel edges). Reject excess degree or an already closed cycle not spanning all vertices. Every remaining component is a path, including isolated vertices. Greedily add the lexicographically smallest edge between available ends of different components; after all components merge, close the final path. Such an edge always has a completion and avoids premature cycles, so the greedy sorted edge multiset is lexicographically minimal. All feasible completions add exactly n-m edges; handle the isolated one-vertex loop and two-vertex double-edge cases uniformly.
review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.
